articles.summary: 海平面上升与气候理想社区
articles.text:
Sea levels are changing rapidly and could rise by 1 metre or more by 2100 without drastic reductions in greenhouse-gas emissions. Low-lying coastal areas-home to nearly one billion people are at high risk of erosion and flooding. In July, for example, torrential rain, coupled with high tides and worsening erosion, inundated coastal areas in Lagos（拉各斯), flooding around2, 000 properties and displacing residents across the Nigerian metropolis.

For coastal communities, urban planning and smart technologies are key to climate adaptation and mitigation. Futuristic designs for flood-resilient settlements or "climatopias", are gaining popularity especially in areas projected to be underwater in a few decades. These large infrastructure projects are being touted by governments and developers as tools to expand the availability of housing, reduce pressures on land, enhance energy efficiency, promote eco- friendly transportation and lessen the effects of flooding.

Critics view them as technological fantasies aimed at growing the value of the property market near oceans and rivers. They also note that climatopias could stifle sustainable adaptations- and we agree that this is a real concern. With the right approach, however, they can be made viable. It is crucial that governments, scientists, environmentalists, think tanks, local communities and ocean-governing agencies evaluate the challenges and benefits of these projects in the short and long term to determine their legitimacy as climate solutions.

Here we offer six criteria by which to assess climatopias during their planning and implementation stages: design type, practicality, ecosystem effects, maladaptation risk, justice concerns and regulatory frameworks.

For design type, unlike the infrastructure in such traditional communities, climatopias are designed to be high-tech cities equipped with solar panels for generating electricity, deep-sea cooling systems, health-care centres, schools, recreational areas and businesses. There are three major ways in which developers are converting ocean and near-shore areas into habitable spaces: reclaimed land, amphibious houses, and floating cities.

In terms of practicality, planners, engineers and environmental specialists must assess the construction materials, structural integrity, safety, cost, market demand and financial sustainability of climatopia projects. Besides, all climatopias are vulnerable to extreme weather- from storms and tsunamis to hurricane-induced floodings--with significant risks of damage and loss of life. To address these problems, governments, planners, insurance companies and affected communities must work together to set industry standards as well as design early-warning systems and evacuation procedures.
articles.reference:
海平面正在迅速上升，如果不大幅减少温室气体排放，到2100 年，海平面可能会上升1 米甚至更多。低洼的沿海地区——居住着近十亿人口—正面临严重的侵蚀和洪水风险。例如，今年7 月，倾盆大雨与高潮潮位及日益加剧的海岸侵蚀共同作用，淹没了拉各斯(Lagos) 沿海区域，约2000 处房屋遭遇洪水，迫使这座尼日利亚大都市的居民流离失所。

对于沿海社区而言，城市规划和智能技术是应对和缓解气候变化的关键。具有防洪能力的未来社区设计，或称为“气候理想社区”(climatopias)，在未来可能被海水淹没的区域越来越受青睐。这些大型基础设施项目被政府和开发商视为扩展住房供应、缓解土地压力、提升能源效率、推动环保交通并减少洪水影响的有效方案。

批评者认为，这些项目是以提升滨海及河岸地段房地产市场价值为目的的技术幻想。他们还指出，气候理想社区可能会抑制可持续的适应措施—而我们也认为这是一个真实的担忧。然而，采用正确的方法，这些项目可以变得切实可行。政府、科学家、环保人士、智库、当地社区和海洋管理机构应当共同评估这些项目在短期和长期内的挑战与益处，以确定它们作为气候解决方案的合法性。

我们提出了六项标准，以用于在气候理想社区的规划和实施阶段进行评估：设计类型、实用性、生态系统影响、不良适应风险、公平性问题以及监管框架。

在设计方面，与传统社区基础设施不同，气候理想社区被构想为高科技城市，配备太阳能发电系统、深海冷却系统、医疗中心、学校、娱乐区域和商业设施。开发商主要通过填海造地、两栖房屋和浮动城市三种方式，将海洋和近岸区域转变为可居住空间。

在实用性方面，规划者、工程师和环境专家必须评估气候理想社区项目的建材选择、结构完整性、安全性、成本、市场需求以及财务可持续性。此外，所有气候理想社区都易受极端天气的威胁——从风暴、海啸到飓风引发的洪水——面临严重的损害和生命风险。为应对这些挑战，政府、规划者、保险公司和受影响的社区必须密切合作，制定行业标准，并设计预警系统和疏散方案。

articles.summary: 服贸会与服务贸易高质量发展
articles.text:
服贸会(CIFTIS)是中国服务业和服务贸易高质量发展的生动写照。今年上半年，中国服务贸易规模创历史新高，服务进出口总额达3.6 万亿元，同比增长14%。中国正以高水平开放推动服务贸易高质量发展，为全球经济发展贡献更大动力。

走进服贸会展区，数字化、智能化、绿色化气息扑面而来。应用人工智能深度学习技术的手术机器人，通过一张CT 片，就能帮医生制定个体化手术方案：电动无人机助力农业生产、巡检、消防提升效率...服贸会上，不少机构和企业首发新技术、新成果，引领行业创新趋势。

作为服务贸易国际合作的重要平台，服贸会着力打造全球服务贸易的“首秀场”。本届服贸会围绕培育发展新质生产力，集中展示了服务贸易数字化、智能化、绿色化发展的最新成果、最新技术和最新应用，陆续发布了200 余项创新成果。
articles.reference:
CIFTIS is a vivid portrayal of the high-quality development of China's service industry and service trade. In the first half of this year, China's service trade scale hit a historical high, with the total volume of service imports and exports reaching 3.6 trillion yuan, marking a 14% increase year-on-year. China is driving the high-quality development of service trade through high-level openness, contributing significantly to global economic growth.

Stepping into the CIFTIS exhibition area, one is immediately enveloped by the essence of digitalization, intelligentization, and greenization. Surgical robots that utilize artificial intelligence deep learning technology can assist doctors in creating personalized surgical plans based on a single CT scan; electric drones enhance efficiency in agricultural production, inspection, and firefighting... At CIFTIS, many institutions and enterprises debut new technologies and achievements, setting the pace for industry innovation trends.

Serving as a vital platform for international cooperation in service trade, CIFTIS strives to establish itself as the “premiere platform”for global service trade. This year's CIFTIS, centered on nurturing the development of new quglity productive forces, has concentrated on displaying the latest outcomes, technologies, and applications in the digitalization, intelligentization, and greenization of service trade, and has sequentially unveiled over 200 innovative achievements.
